newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Iberia ended 1996 with 3.5 bln pta profit.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Iberia ended 1996 with 3.5 bln pta profit.

text.p: Spanish state airline company Iberia said on Friday it closed 1996 with consolidated profit of around 3.5 billion pesetas.
It also expects to end 1997 with a consolidated profit of around 11 billion pesetas versus a loss of around 44.92 billion pesetas in 1995.

In 1996 the Spanish government injected 87 billion pesetas in fresh money through a capital increase aimed at a global overhaul. A further 20 billion pesetas are expected to be added to its capital as soon as Brussels gives the go-ahead.
At a press conference Iberia Chairman Xabier de Irala presented the airline's new three-year overhaul plan, expected to boost operating profit to 48.9 billion pesetas in 1999.
Iberia expects revenues to rise to 641 billion pesetas in 1999, with expenditures at 592 billion pesetas.
According to its plan, Iberia does not intend to cut business areas or to reduce its staff, Irala told reporters.
"The strategic plan is not to cut any business," he said.
Iberia intends to invest between 300 and 600 billion pesetas in the next three years.
About its troubled Venezuelan airline Viasa, Iberia said little remains to save it from bankruptcy if the Venezuelan government do not decide to inject funds.
Iberia has a 45 percent stake in Viasa.
